register.level: gentle, practical, slightly grown-up English of a well-read clergyman-scholar's daughter in her mid-teens (h1_summary §1)
register.summary: The only fully waking voice. Warm and indulgent ('dear') but already speaking like a young woman in charge: she humours the dream, then turns Alice home to tea. Only two lines in the source, so beyond them the card is designed (inferred:true) for any new waking-frame lines dialogue-rewrite may need (ev0001 opening, ev0053–ev0054 close).

examples.text: Wake up, Alice dear! Why, what a long sleep you've had!
It was a curious dream, dear, certainly: but now run in to your tea; it's getting late.

sentence_style.length: short to medium (mean 14 words), complete and well-formed; affectionate opener, then a practical instruction

patterns.rule: Endearment attached to the name or tacked on mid-sentence ('Alice dear', ', dear,').

examples.text: It was a curious dream, dear, certainly:

patterns.rule: Indulge, then redirect: she concedes Alice's point ('certainly') and follows with 'but now' plus a household instruction tied to the time of day.

examples.text: … but now run in to your tea; it's getting late.

patterns.rule: Inferred for new waking-frame lines: brief, book-reader's replies that do not look up from the page, such as a mild hush or a gentle correction. No questions of wonder: she is the calm reference point against which the dream is measured.
patterns.reason: the source gives her no opening lines (ch001-p01 shows her only reading a book 'without pictures or conversations'); designed from ch001-p01, ch012-p27..p29 and the SUP-001 frame so that dialogue-rewrite has a rule for ev0001 lines

examples.text: (prose) once or twice she had peeped into the book her sister was reading, but it had no pictures or conversations in it
Why, what a long sleep you've had!

preferred_fields: gentle adult judgement of a child's talk ('a curious dream')

examples.text: It was a curious dream, dear, certainly

address.self: I (inferred; she never uses a first person in the source)
address.reason: only two source lines, both addressed to Alice; first-person usage is designed

forbidden_words.domain: Wonderland catchphrases in the waking voice
forbidden_words.regex: \b(curiouser|off with|we're all mad|the moral of|oh my ears|I shall be late|twinkle)\b
forbidden_words.reason: SUP-001 / ruling 5.3 B: the waking frame stays realistic; the sister only glimpses the dream at the trial and never speaks its idioms (she may call it 'a curious dream', which is her own adult word)
those mark Alice; the sister is the composed elder

drift.change: No drift in her own voice: she is the fixed waking reference at the opening (reading, silent in the source) and the close (ch012). What changes is Alice's view of her, not her speech.
drift.reason: she has no lines before ch012; the opening-reading behaviour is taken from prose ch001-p01

backtest_markers.regex: \b(run in|your tea|getting late|wake up|long sleep|but now)\b

backtest.method: marker-claim back-test: a spoken source line hits when it matches >=1 backtest_markers regex and no forbidden_words regex; verse (recited text) excluded; full definition runs/p3-dialogue-style-pb1/result.json#backtest_method
